column1: Vetus EC4 (Flexball) engine-control CAN bus: observed codes and timings
Draft v0.2, 6 Oct 2026. Dr.FireFly. Rows held pending disclosure to the manufacturers are not included.

column2: An independent, listen-only decode of the CAN bus of a Vetus EC4 electronic engine control (Flexball 4500 actuators), twin engines, two twin-lever stations (main helm and flybridge). Every value was observed on one installation; other installations, firmware versions or settings may differ.
Fairline Phantom 42, twin engines. Owner-installed EC4; every EC4 parameter at factory default (shift delays dI and dA both 0.0 s).

Listen-only sniffer (ESP32 with an isolated ISO1050 transceiver, controller in listen-only mode, never transmits, no termination) on a T-junction drop of the EC4 bus. Frames timestamped on receipt (firmware rev D.2) and written to SD as candump text. Test steps typed as timestamped notes from a phone during the captures. Engines off for every capture.
Three captures, 23 Sep, 27 Sep and 2 Oct 2026; 71,094 frames, 38 minutes in all. See the Captures and log sheet.

Measured = seen directly in a capture, with a labelled test step where stated. Inferred = follows from the captures but not directly tested. Manual = from the Vetus EC4 manual 030624.13 (2024), not from the bus.
Now = published with the receive-side decode. Hold = held pending disclosure to the manufacturers; those rows are not in this folder.

Lever time = receipt time of the first station frame (0x181 or 0x282) showing the new gear byte. Actuator times are receipt times of the actuator frames (0x384, 0x485), which arrive every 153.6 ms, so any actuator time is quantised to about one actuator period. Times are engines-off: with engines running, gear loads and RPM decay may change them.
